issue: PMAT-574 (closes forjar#574) — release 1.31.0. Five PRs since v1.30.0, three of which change behaviour: drift's verdict reaches the exit code (PMAT-562, #563), a run that inspected none of the resources it was asked about declines with exit 2 (PMAT-564, #569), and a service is converged only while the loaded unit executes the declared program (PMAT-560, #568). The first two are the two signatures of paiml/infra#605. No Rust is changed by this cut: the diff is the version, the record of what shipped, and the ledger bookkeeping the release gates demanded.

quorum.judges_note: THE BINDING JUDGES ON THIS CUT ARE NOT THE LANES. Three of the four refutations came from instruments that ruled before any lane saw the branch: gate H refused the crux rows (backticks inside the key span it greps), the commit-msg hook refused a cut commit whose ticket said completed, and reading README.md refuted the receipt's claim that its version lines were already correct. The fourth came from lane 1. judges=3 counts the three lanes that were ASKED, of which one returned a verdict; it is not three independent tiers and must not be read as such. .quorum/evidence/release-1.31.0-judges.md names each refuting authority.

refuted_claims: R1: 'the README's version lines are already correct' — the first draft of the impl receipt said README.md was untouched; the file said forjar = "1.30" on lines 96 and 98. Both now say 1.31. Gate D passed either way, because Cargo reads 1.30 as >=1.30.0, <2.0.0, which is why nothing else would have caught it.

R2: 'the cut's own ticket can be marked completed in the cut's own PR' — refused by the commit-msg hook: 'Pmat-Ticket PMAT-574 is completed — work belongs to an open item, and CB-2113 refuses this commit in CI'. PMAT-574 stays inprogress; the booking PR closes it.

R3: 'the crux rows are written, so gate H is satisfied' — GATE H FAIL 3 behaviour bullet(s) under [1.31.0] have no row. The rows existed but carried backticks inside the span the gate greps as a FIXED string.
R4: 'the receipt's diff list is complete' — lane 1, cited: it named the dogfood receipt and the cut log but not the receipt doing the listing, nor the quorum artifacts.

falsification.test: falsification_release_changelog_counts_the_window is the falsifier this cut RESTS on rather than one it adds: it is what makes the CHANGELOG window rule refutable, and this cut is an instance of that rule. No new test is owed, because the diff changes no Rust — gate F reports no .rs differs from origin/main. The three behaviours being released were each falsified on their own branch: #563 (drift's exit code), #569 (six cases through the binary, 5 RED on the unfixed source), #568 (a fake systemctl printing what systemd 249 prints, RED 8 of 10 on 1.30.0).

crux.verdict: docs/audits/crux-1.31.0.md, three rows, one per behaviour bullet, each naming >= 3 of the 28 surveyed systems. Written by the release orchestrator from documentation memory rather than surveyed by an agy lane as 1.29.0's was, every third-party claim marked [X], and the audit's Method section says so in its first paragraph. It also states what is NOT reconciled: PMAT-565 was still open at the cut, so its behaviour owes no row.
systems: Bazel, Ansible, Terraform, Kubernetes: a selection that matches nothing is an error in Bazel and in modern Ansible's --limit, while kubectl prints 'No resources found' and exits 0 [X] — forjar had the kubectl shape, and worse, because its empty selection still graded two resources from another manifest

systemd, Ansible, Puppet, Chef, Podman: systemd distinguishes the unit file on disk from the unit it has loaded [X]; the configuration managers all converge on state/enabled and manage the unit FILE separately [X]; the container world identifies what runs by DIGEST [X], which is what exec_sha256 is

Terraform, Puppet, Kubernetes, Ansible: -detailed-exitcode (2), --detailed-exitcodes (2) and kubectl diff (1) all put a difference in the exit code [X], while ansible --check exits 0 and makes you parse the recap [X] — forjar's verdict was real but flag-gated, which is an un-gated bug for every caller that did not know the flag
